subject: Request: remediation payout & authorization after sustained latency (Cloudlys)
messages:
From: Beth Sanders <beth@cloudlys.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: support@cloudlys.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sustained latency last week — request for remediation plan and payout

Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick troubleshooting yesterday. To recap from our side: between 2027-04-13 02:10 UTC and 2027-04-14 15:30 UTC our production inference pipelines saw elevated tail latency (P99 spiked to ~1.9s) and an intermittent 503 for a subset of model shards. This impacted two customer-facing features: contextual suggestions and search re-ranking.

We're collecting downstream impact metrics but preliminary estimates are ~5% lost completions during the window and about $18k in incremental customer support cost for that week. Given our contract (SLA section 4.2), we'd like to open a remediation request and discuss a one-off payout or service credit to offset the operational cost and customer goodwill outreach.

Can you confirm what remedial options Redwood can provide (credit structure, timeline, any documentation we need to close this out)? We may need approvals from our procurement/legal team depending on structure.

Appreciate it — Beth

Beth Sanders
VP Product Operations | Cloudlys
beth@cloudlys.com
+1 (415) 555-0189
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Beth Sanders <beth@cloudlys.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sustained latency last week — request for remediation plan and payout

Beth — thanks for the details and the timeline. I'm really sorry for the disruption. We own this one and want to make the remediation straightforward.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- We're attaching an incident timeline and a proposed compensation worksheet (sending internally for approval in parallel).
- We'll validate the downstream completion-loss metrics with your engineering contact if you can share the customer-facing logs (redacted).
- Proposed remedial options (subject to exec approval): a) service credit equal to 15% of April usage; b) $20k one-time operational goodwill payout; c) three months of prioritized support for the affected feature rollout.

I'll loop in Lauren and Aditya to get approval routing and to confirm the financial and contract implications. Expect an internal proposal later today.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sustained latency — internal: recommendation & approval ask

Karthik / Aditya — forwarding Beth's note plus the incident timeline. Summary of our recommended settlement is below (finance and legal flagged items in bold):

Summary recommendation:
- Offer a blended remediation package: 12% service credit for April invoice + $15k one-time credit to offset support costs + two months free Dedicated burst capacity (for their reindex job), delivered as account creditable SKUs.
- Require Cloudlys to acknowledge incident closure via an acceptance email and refrain from public statements for 30 days (legal requested minimal PR language).
- No SLA amendment; this is a one-off goodwill settlement.

Why this structure? It balances showing contrition while keeping exposure predictable. The $15k one-time credit is below our CFO threshold for exec signoff; anything > $25k will need VP/Sales CFO approval.

Attachments: proposed_compensation_sheet.xlsx (internal worksheet with line items).

Can you confirm approval to proceed with this package and authorize me to issue the credits? If you want a different mix (bigger cash component vs credit), note that will change approval level required.

- Lauren
Director, Customer Success Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sustained latency — internal: recommendation & approval ask

Lauren / Karthik — I support the blended package as structured. Two quick notes:
1) Finance: we can issue the 12% invoice credit + the $15k account credit without VP signature, provided we mark it as a one-off goodwill settlement and tie it to the incident ticket number. I'll prepare the accounting memo.
2) Ops: before we finalize, operations would like to include a short runbook (post-incident) and a small service-level commitment: for one month after remediation we'll provide weekly latency reports and prioritized on-call for their integration. This helps Cloudlys rebuild confidence and reduces the probability of churn.

Approve to proceed on my side. Lauren, please prepare the credit paperwork and the acceptance wording for Beth.

— Aditya
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Beth Sanders <beth@cloudlys.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, legal@cloudlys.com
Date: Fri, 22 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Settlement proposal for April latency incident (Cloudlys)

Beth — thanks for your patience while we coordinated internally. Below is what Redwood can offer as a one-off remediation package; this is intended to be a fast path to closure and to get your teams back to product work.

Proposed remediation package (one-off):
- 12% service credit applied to the April 2027 invoice (will appear as a line-item credit on next invoice).
- $15,000 account credit applied to Cloudlys billing account (usable for Dedicated or Console add-ons).
- Two months of Dedicated burst capacity (no charge), applied as SKUs to support your reindex and peak traffic periods.
- One month of weekly latency & performance reports + prioritized incident routing (Ops-runbook handover).

Next steps if you accept:
1) Please reply with a short acceptance line (e.g., "Cloudlys accepts the remediation package as outlined").
2) We'll issue the invoice credit and account credit within 7 business days after acceptance.
3) We'll schedule the Ops handover and provide the first weekly report within 5 business days.

Attachments: incident_timeline.pdf, proposed_compensation_sheet.xlsx

If Cloudlys would prefer a higher cash component instead of credits, let me know and we'll advise on the approval path (anything with > $25k cash requires VP/CFO signoff).

Appreciate the partnership and sorry again for the impact — we'll follow up on the runbook and the first latency report immediately after you accept.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
